chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: What a black and tan club was; graft in prejudiced Chicago
summary: Willard defines a black and tan as welcoming both races, and Collins says prejudiced Chicago was also graft-ridden, so almost anything could be bought off.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I shouldn't of facetiously cut you off about black and tan. Maybe it should go on the record. Black and tan club was one where all black and white patrons were welcome.
There were a lot of clubs where (inaudible) they weren't.

They weren't welcome. In Chicago was a terribly prejudiced town, very prejudiced town. But always a graft ridden town. You know, there was always that graft, so you could pay off and do almost anything you wanted. As a matter of fact Gloria Swanson came in to see Gloria Swanson.
